summary: Chapter 17 begins with damaged performance audio and a sick participant whose mask, distance and contact boundaries are handled inconsistently. It continues the private Aaliyah relationship, revisits the prior surprise and rib injury, and ranges across adult-industry labor, deceptive-production ideas, film criticism, a private transactional-sex encounter, property snooping and deliberate contamination. A guest reports a severe Fusobacterium necrophorum infection; the room then offers unreliable parasite remedies. The episode's central evidentiary section is a guest's first-person account of intercourse after an intoxicated man repeatedly says he does not want sex, pushes her off, says stop and please, and never says yes. She says she proceeded anyway; his erection, penetration and later reaction do not retroactively establish freely given consent. The room both identifies and minimizes this, and separately discusses sexual contact with an unconscious person. CDC definitions contradict claims that women cannot rape men and recognize being made to penetrate without consent. Later sections cover a fan couple, Filipino fandom and a proposed Philippines production trip, unsupported semen and health claims, and likely Melanotan II injections obtained from the UK. FDA identifies Melanotan II as an unapproved injectable tanning drug; new dark spots are not proof of safe efficacy. The closing trivia game repeatedly dismisses intimate-contact refusals before a participant eventually offers contact; each contemporaneous boundary controls. Every idea, explicit detail, slur and contradiction remains in the source transcript. Editorial navigation adds context and restricts reidentification, medical misinformation and coercive how-to value without censoring the record. No line-level speaker names publish because acoustic identity windows remain unvalidated.

source_notes.claim: Erection, penetration or later participation indicates consent.
source_notes.assessment: false; CDC defines consent through words or overt actions indicating freely given agreement and recognizes inability to consent while asleep, unconscious or incapacitated.

source_notes.claim: It is impossible for a woman to rape a man.
source_notes.assessment: false; CDC explicitly recognizes sexual violence against all sexes and being made to penetrate without consent.

source_notes.claim: Natural membrane and synthetic nonlatex condoms are interchangeable for STI prevention.
source_notes.assessment: false; CDC says natural-membrane condoms should not be used to prevent HIV or other STIs.

source_notes.claim: Warm milk or visual inspection is a sufficient pinworm diagnosis/remedy.
source_notes.assessment: unsupported; CDC recommends clinician involvement and describes a three-morning tape test.

source_notes.claim: The imported injectable tanning drug is legal and its dark-spot effects prove it works safely.
source_notes.assessment: the product is likely but not certainly Melanotan II; FDA identifies Melanotan II as an unapproved injectable tanning drug and did not recognize it as safe and effective.
